newsitem.title: INDONESIA: NEC officially opens Indonesia plant.
newsitem.headline: NEC officially opens Indonesia plant.

text.p: NEC Corporation of Japan and and an Indonesian firm controlled by President Suharto's youngest son formally inaugurated a $45 million joint venture semiconductor plant on Tuesday.

"The plant started the production of signal transistors and linear integrated circuits (ICs) in January 1997 with one million pieces of ICs per month. We gradually increased the production up to 15 million ICs per month by May," NEC President Hisashi Kaneko said at the inauguration ceremony.
The joint venture, called PT NEC Humpuss Semiconductors Indonesia, has located the plant in the town of Cikarang near Jakarta.
Kaneko said that by the end of 1997, the company expected to produce 48 million signal transistors and 6 million linear ICs.

"The increase of output also increases sales. Annual sales will reach $40 million in the financial year 2000," he said. The company has targetted annual production of 111 million signal transistors and 19 million ICs by that time.
Signal transistors and linear ICs are used in personal computers, televisions, video recorders and other home electronic products.
The joint venture was established in September 1995 with an authorised capital of $15.4 million.

NEC controls a 65 percent stake in the joint venture, PT Humpuss Elektronika of the Humpuss group -- controlled by Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra -- owns 25 percent while the remaining 10 percent is owned by Sumitomo Corporation of Japan.
"With this plant, NEC investment in Indonesia now exceeds $100 million," Kaneko said.
